glance_takeaway: Fernwick is choosing a vector-search engine for semantic product search (4.1M vectors doubling yearly, 120 QPS). Four candidates were benchmarked; two (pgnearest, Braid) fail must-have requirements and are crossed out, leaving Quiver (managed SaaS, ~zero ops but pricier/locked-in) versus Hearth (self-hosted OSS, cheaper long-run but needs engineers). There's no outright winner - the recommendation is an IF/THEN: if a platform hire signs by the 2026-10-01 checkpoint, go Hearth (self-hosted); otherwise Quiver with a mandatory exit plan, and a red 'override' warns that heavy filtered traffic or very low selectivity flips the decision to Quiver regardless.

F1.note: Top gate strip: 'M1 p95 <=100 ms at 10M incl. 30% filtered / M2 recall@10 >=0.92 / M3 filtered recall >=0.90 at 5% selectivity / M4 EU data residency / M5 <=$2,500/mo at ~10M vectors' - all five, correct.

F2.note: Header: '4.1M vectors doubling yearly, 120 QPS peak, 30% of queries filtered'; M5 line notes '~10M vectors (12-month scale)'; chart axis to 100M with 'corpus has doubled every year'; override box: 'Filter share is trending up.'

F3.note: Partial: 'two-week bakeoff at 10M vectors' is stated, but the methodology (June 2026, frozen dataset, identical hardware, 48-hour log replay at 120 QPS, brute-force ground truth) is absent; a reader learns the bakeoff existed but not why it is trustworthy.

F4.note: Partial: page reports filtered p95 (Quiver 22, Hearth 48, pgnearest 110) instead of the unfiltered figures (18/41/95); only Braid's 12 ms and 'Braid is fastest' + 'both clear M1 with room' survive; correctly labeled so not contradictory, but the F4 numbers are not on the page.

F5.note: Partial: Braid 0.98 and pgnearest 0.89 (fails M2) appear; survivors' unfiltered recall (Quiver 0.97, Hearth 0.94) is absent - page gives their filtered recall instead.

F6.note: pgnearest card: '110 ms filtered p95 - fails M1 (<=100 ms)' and 'recall@10 0.89 - fails M2 (>=0.92); an index ceiling, not tuning', with red strikethrough and 'x M1 M2' badge.

F7.note: Braid card: '12 ms p95, recall 0.98 - best raw numbers in the bakeoff', 'post-hoc filter recall 0.71 @5% - fails M3 (>=0.90)', 'structural, not tunable - the index ignores metadata'.

F8.note: Both cards carry PASS badges; Hearth: 'recall 0.90 @5% - at the M3 floor', '0.86 @1% sel.'; Quiver: 'recall 0.96 @5%, 0.95 @1% sel.' (0.96 at 5% vs key_facts' 0.95-at-1% claim is consistent).

F9.note: Chart: Quiver '$180' at 1M vs Hearth '$520 HA floor (covers to ~5M)'; script step 5: 'Quiver cheapest at 1M'. Eliminated options' 1M prices ($240/$210) omitted - minor, they are out of the race by then.

F10.note: Chart labels: '$1,400' vs '$1,900' at 10M with 'M5 cap $2,500 @10M' dashed line; at 100M '$6,800 - 3.4x cheaper' vs '$23,000 (Enterprise tier >50M)'. pgnearest/Braid 100M estimates absent (already eliminated).

F11.note: 'infra crossover ~3M - behind us' marker; dashed 'Hearth + ops labor (~$2,800/mo, ~0.2 FTE)' curve with 'labor-adjusted crossover ~30M vectors ~ 2029'. Log-scale positions check out.

F12.note: Quiver: '~0 FTE ops (vendor on-call, 99.9% SLA)'; Hearth: '~0.2 FTE + >=4-eng on-call'; IF box: 'PLAT-7 infra hire has signed and started (req approved today - not yet filled)'. Only the ~0.5 FTE first-quarter ramp is omitted.

F13.note: Quiver card: 'lock-in high / in-VPC: never'; tradeoff box: '(in-VPC likely needed for 2027 enterprise contracts)'; Hearth 'low lock-in'; exit plan carries 'standing ~3 engineer-week migration budget'. Proprietary DSL not named explicitly but implied by the SearchIndex-adapter bullet.

F14.note: Green recommendation box reproduces the full conditional: IF PLAT-7 signed+started and >=4-eng on-call committed by 2026-10-01 -> Hearth primary; ELSE Quiver with SearchIndex adapter, quarterly JSONL export drill into a scratch Hearth, ~3 engineer-week budget, re-evaluate at 30M or first renewal.

F15.note: Red 'Standing override - S1' box: filtered >60% or selectivity <2% -> Quiver even if the hire lands, 'Hearth's 0.90 filtered recall has no margin'; timeline shows 2026-10-01 headcount checkpoint and 2027-01-15 full review.

render_issues: Minor label collisions in the rendered frame: chart legend text is clipped by the right-hand panel ('self-hosted, infra [only]' and '(~$2,80[0/mo...]' cut off); the 'x M1 M2' badge overlaps the pgnearest subtitle; the '$1,900' label collides with the M5-cap dashed line; 'today: 4.1M' crowds the '$ / month (log)' axis label. Nothing is broken, but several annotations require squinting.
strengths: The conditional structure - the hardest part of this test case - is fully explicit and visually segregated: green IF/THEN box, red standing-override box, and a dated checkpoint timeline; a reader can answer 'what would change your mind?' without re-reading.
Elimination logic is unmistakable: red strikethroughs with per-must-have failure badges (x M1 M2, x M3) make 'out on requirements, not taste' legible even at a glance.

The cost chart is honest and complete: log-log with correct positional encoding, both crossovers marked (~3M infra 'behind us', ~30M labor-adjusted ~2029), the M5 cap drawn in, and the renewal-risk caveat footnoted.
Graceful degradation: the final frame is the no-JS default, so the static screenshot carries the entire argument, and the 8-step script doubles as a readable narrative fallback.
weaknesses: Bakeoff methodology is nearly absent (48-hour log replay, frozen dataset, identical hardware, brute-force ground truth) - the reader must take the numbers on faith (F3).
The page substitutes filtered p95/recall for the unfiltered benchmark table, so three of the four F4 latencies and two of the four F5 recall values never appear (F4, F5 distorted).
Label crowding in the chart center: clipped legend, overlapping annotations, and a badge covering card text - small but repeated legibility taxes on an otherwise dense single screen.
The 'benchmarks would pick the wrong option' lesson (T4) lives mostly in the Braid card fine print and script step 3; it does not surface at glance strength the way the IF/THEN does.
evaluator_notes: Motion/build-up page whose default (JS-off) state is the finished final frame, so glance == full screenshot. Fact audit: 12 conveyed, 3 distorted, 0 contradicted -> accuracy = 10*12/15 = 8.0. Glance pass landed T1 and T2 completely (including the standing override), T3 partially (direction of the cost inversion but not the crossovers), T4 only as 'two eliminated on must-haves'. Overall = 0.35*8.0 + 0.30*7.5 + 0.15*7.5 + 0.10*8.0 + 0.10*7.0 = 7.7.
